query: My pharmacist says irbesartan isn't funded. Can I still get it through my doctor?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Irbesartan (not funded, Section 29 unapproved)" Old: the entry said only that irbesartan is not funded in New Zealand, with no mention that it is an unapproved medicine.

query: I'm on ramipril for my kidneys and I have a bad chest infection with low oxygen. Should I keep taking it?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Withhold temporarily in any condition where tissue hypoperfusion and hypoxia may be a problem e.g., cardiac or respiratory failure, myocardial infarction (MI), dehydration, or serious infection." Old: the entry listed dehydration, heart failure, serious infection and heart attack, and left out respiratory failure and the low blood flow or oxygen rationale.

query: I have atrial fibrillation and I just fainted at home. Is that something I can raise at my next check-up?
notes: Safety. New raw: "Request acute general medicine assessment, regardless of the length of time AF has been present, if: chest pain. symptomatic hypotension. new or worsened heart failure. syncope." Old: the entry said to go to the emergency department or call an ambulance; the new entry gives 111 and the same list.

query: I take aspirin and clopidogrel after my heart stent. Do I still need a blood thinner for my atrial fibrillation?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Dual antiplatelet therapy has bleeding risks similar to oral anticoagulants, and is less effective at stroke prevention." Old: the entry covered aspirin alone; it did not say that two antiplatelet medicines carry bleeding risk like anticoagulants and prevent stroke less well.

query: I take amiodarone and the vision in one eye suddenly went blurry and sore. Can I wait until my next blood test to mention it?
notes: Safety. New raw: "Request acute ophthalmology assessment" Old: the entry said optic neuritis requires urgent assessment, with no 111 or emergency department action.

query: I'm on amiodarone and my doctor has added eplerenone for heart failure. What is the highest dose I should be on?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Use with caution in the elderly and those on amiodarone – the recommended maximum dose is 25 mg daily." Old: eplerenone was not covered in the entry.

query: My blood test shows potassium of 6.7 and the practice says they will sort it out next week. Should I just wait?
notes: Safety. New raw: "Potassium 6.5 or more – potential medical emergency." Old: the entry said same-day advice would be sought, with no 111 or emergency department action for the patient.

query: My creatinine rose 40% after I started my ACE inhibitor and it was stopped. If my kidneys recover, will I restart at the same dose?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Withhold ACE inhibitor or ARB and reassess creatinine at 2 to 4 weeks. If improvement: Reintroduce at half dose" Old: the entry said only that the medicine is reintroduced at a lower dose once stable, with no 2 to 4 week recheck or half dose.

query: Can I take my rivaroxaban 20 mg on an empty stomach in the morning?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Advise patient to take rivaroxaban with food. Bioavailability is reduced to approximately 66% if taken on an empty stomach, compared with over 99% if taken with a meal." Old: the entry said only 'with food', with no absorption figures.

query: I have a heart stent and take aspirin. Do I have to stop the aspirin when I start dabigatran?
notes: Changed. New raw: "In a patient with ischaemic heart disease, both aspirin or clopidogrel and dabigatran or warfarin are likely to be needed, especially if they have had coronary surgery or stenting." Old: the entry said aspirin is usually stopped when dabigatran starts and to discuss with your doctor if you have ischaemic heart disease or a stent; the new entry says both may be needed and, if bleeding risk is high, to treat the most serious condition or seek specialist advice.

query: My HbA1c came back at 49. Do I count as having diabetes now?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Diabetes – HbA1c 48 mmol/mol or greater (lowered from the current 50 mmol/mol or greater)" Old: the old raw said type 2 diabetes is diagnosed at HbA1c 50 mmol/mol or above, with no confirmatory-test rule for 48 to 52.

query: I was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes with an HbA1c of 50, and my HbA1c a year ago was normal. When should I have my first eye screening?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Refer for retinal screening in 3 years if confirmed diabetes with HbA1c 48 to 52 mmol/mol, and clear onset within the last 2 years" Old: type 2 diabetes screening started at diagnosis for everyone.

query: My knee is red, hot and very painful, I have a fever and my heart is racing. I've had gout before, so is it fine to book my GP for next week?
notes: Safety. New raw: "If septic arthritis is the most likely diagnosis, do not delay hospital transfer by performing joint aspiration in primary care." Old: the entry said to get same-day or urgent medical review, with no 111 or emergency department action.

query: My doctor wants me to take colchicine for gout, but my grandchildren stay at my house a lot. Is that a problem?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Avoid if there are any children or people vulnerable to overdose in the patient's environment." Old: the entry said only to keep colchicine out of reach and ask for child-proof packaging; it did not say colchicine is avoided when children are in the household.

query: I'm on warfarin and I've had a new headache that is different from my usual ones and getting worse. Should I just take paracetamol?
notes: Safety. New raw: "Significant new headache, or change to previous headache pattern, and any of the following risk factors:"; "Anticoagulation or dual antiplatelet therapy" Old: the entry listed only 'new or different headache if you are over 50' and told patients to go to the emergency department or call an ambulance.

query: I'm 30 and on the pill. My doctor suggested topiramate to prevent migraines. Is there anything I need to know about contraception?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Emphasise the importance of effective contraception e.g., contraceptive injection, an intrauterine device (IUD), or combined oral contraceptive (COC) with a barrier method." Old: the entry said topiramate is contraindicated in pregnancy and needs a pregnancy test, with no mention of barrier contraception.

query: My TSH is still high even though I take 200 micrograms of thyroxine. What happens next?
notes: Changed. New raw: "If TSH remains elevated despite titrating thyroxine to 200 micrograms per day, check adherence and advise the patient to take it on an empty stomach 1 hour before breakfast. Recheck in 6 to 8 weeks and seek endocrinology advice if TSH is still elevated." Old: the entry said only that specialist advice is sought if TSH stays high at maximum dose with confirmed adherence, with no empty stomach advice or 6 to 8 week recheck.

query: A friend takes natural thyroid extract. Should I swap my levothyroxine for it, or add T3?
notes: Changed. New raw: "There is no robust evidence that shows a benefit of such products, or the addition of T3 to T4." Old: the entry said natural extracts are not recommended and are harder to monitor; it did not address adding T3.

query: My ANA blood test came back positive at 1 in 160 and I have no other symptoms. Does that mean I have lupus?
notes: Changed. New raw: "An ANA of 1 in 160 is found in 5% of the normal population, more in females and in the older population." Old: the entry did not give the ANA 1 in 160 figure.

query: My GP wants to start prednisone for my joint inflammation while I wait to see the rheumatologist. What dose is usual and how is it reduced?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Start prednisone 15 to 20 mg daily for 2 to 4 weeks. After 2 to 4 weeks, decrease by 5 mg every 2 to 4 weeks and titrate to lowest dose patient can tolerate." Old: the entry said 15 to 20 mg daily, then gradually reduced over weeks.

query: I work rotating shifts and want to nap before driving home. How long should my naps be?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Naps should be 40 minutes or less." Old: the entry did not cover shift work napping.

query: I do night shifts and want to use coffee to stay alert. How much caffeine is sensible?
notes: Changed. New raw: "start with 100 mg and titrate up as needed"; "avoid using more than 300 mg a day so sleep is not adversely affected" Old: the entry did not cover caffeine for shift work.

query: My pharmacist says Protaphane is being discontinued. What will I be switched to, and will my dose change?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Supply of Protaphane will be discontinued at the end of 2026. The most like-for-like alternative is Humulin NPH and patients can be switched over to the same dose, but they will require a Savvio pen." Old: the entry said only that Protaphane is being discontinued in 2026 and to switch to Humulin NPH; it gave no dose or pen advice.

query: NovoMix 30 is being discontinued and my doctor mentioned Ryzodeg. Will my dose stay the same?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Supply of NovoMix 30 will also likely be discontinued at the end of 2026. The most like-for-like alternatives are Humalog Mix 25 (requires Savvio pen)" Old: the entry said only that NovoMix 30 is being discontinued in 2026, with no replacement or dose advice.

query: I've been on pregabalin for six weeks and my nerve pain hasn't changed. Should I keep going?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Start at a low dose and increase, if required, especially if there is partial response. Stop if no improvement after a trial of one month." Old: the entry did not give a one month trial limit for gabapentinoids.

query: Why does my pharmacy give me my gabapentin only one month at a time?
notes: Changed. New raw: "monthly dispensing instead of every 3 months in general" Old: the entry said dispensing may be weekly for higher-risk people, with no monthly dispensing for gabapentinoids in general.

query: When should I put on sunscreen and how often should I reapply?
notes: Changed. New raw: "at least 20 minutes before going outside, 10 to 20 minutes after going outside and every 2 hours after that." Old: the entry said SPF 50+ applied 20 minutes before going outside and reapplied every 2 hours, with no application after going outside.

query: Nodular melanoma sounds rare. Why do doctors worry about it so much?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Approximately 15% of all melanomas are nodular melanomas, but they comprise more than 60% of melanomas > 3 mm in thickness." Old: the entry gave 'over 60% of thick melanomas' without the 15% share or the 3 mm cut-off.

query: I keep going to the after-hours clinic and sometimes the emergency department for my asthma. Does that mean anything?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Frequent attenders for emergency treatment (general practice, after hour surgeries, emergency departments)" Old: the entry listed hospital admissions and emergency department visits in the past year, but not frequent attendance at general practice and after-hours clinics.

query: Should I replace the carpets and buy mite-proof covers to control my asthma?
notes: Changed. New raw: "House dust mites – The available avoidance strategies are labour- and cost-intensive, and don't significantly alter asthma control." Old: the entry said avoidance is labour-intensive and may not significantly alter control, with no mention of cost.

query: I have insomnia and think I might have sleep apnoea. Is a home overnight oximetry test a good idea?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Patients with insomnia may also have confusing results from a basic sleep test." Old: the entry said to avoid the basic home test if you have insomnia, without saying why; the new entry says results can be confusing.

query: Can I use Otrivine nasal spray every night for my blocked nose and snoring?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Otrivine, 1 to 2 sprays at night – maximum duration 1 week to avoid rebound congestion" Old: the entry did not give the Otrivine and nasal steroid course lengths.

query: My feet went numb over two days and now my legs feel weak and it seems to be spreading upwards. Should I book a GP appointment for next week?
notes: Safety. New raw: "Acute onset or rapid progression is uncommon and suggests Guillain-Barré syndrome, vasculitis, or toxins, and usually needs acute admission." Old: the entry called it a medical emergency needing urgent assessment, with no 111 or emergency department action.

query: How do I use capsaicin cream for the nerve pain in my feet? Should I rub it in well?
notes: Changed. New raw: "to use regularly 3 to 4 times a day. Do not massage in." Old: the entry said apply 3 to 4 times daily and wash hands, and described the 0.075% cream as funded; the new entry says to use it regularly and not on broken skin.

query: I fainted while jogging yesterday and feel fine today. Do I need to do anything about it?
notes: Safety. New raw: "Exertional syncope" Old: the entry said you need urgent assessment; the new entry says to call 111 or go to the emergency department.

query: I fainted when I stood up after starting a new blood pressure tablet, and my doctor stopped it. Can I drive again?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Likewise for a patient newly started on antihypertensives who has postural syncope and the triggering medication is withdrawn." Old: the entry gave stand-down rules by cause but did not cover fainting from a new blood pressure medicine that has been stopped.

query: My 2-month-old's vitamin D level came back at 20 nmol/L. What treatment is usual?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Younger than 3 months | Less than 25 nmol/L | 800 units (2 drops) a day for 3 months" Old: under 6 months with a level below 30 nmol/L, the entry gave 2000 units (5 drops) daily for 3 months.

query: My toddler's vitamin D is low and the lab note says corrected calcium is 1.9, but he seems perfectly well. Can we wait for the doctor to review it next week?
notes: Safety. New raw: "Corrected calcium < 2 mmol/L May be asymptomatic. Hypocalcaemia is a life-threatening condition, with the potential for rapid deterioration." Old: the entry said urgent hospital assessment; the new entry says call 111 or go to the emergency department even if the child has no symptoms.

query: My baby is mostly formula fed but only drinks about 300 mL a day. Does she need vitamin D drops?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Infants who are exclusively breastfed or receive less than 500 mL of formula a day are recommended to receive vitamin D supplementation before age 4 weeks" Old: the entry said exclusively breastfed infants need supplementation from before 4 weeks, with no formula volume threshold.

query: Is my multivitamin enough to cover my vitamin D?
notes: Changed. New raw: "Many multivitamin preparations (funded and unfunded) do not provide sufficient colecalciferol unless excessive doses of other vitamins (e.g. vitamin A) are taken." Old: the entry said many multivitamins lack enough vitamin D unless taken in excess; the new entry names vitamin A as the excess risk and adds that plain vitamin D is available over the counter.
